fields.label: Value
fields.description: Formatted for reading. A dash means the measure had no sample to compute from -- which is not zero, and must not be read as one.

fields.label: Coverage
fields.description: Whether the value means anything. Tracked: the source is in use. Not Tracked: the source holds no rows anywhere on this site, so a zero means nobody records this. No Source: nothing on this site could ever record it.

fields.label: Verdict
fields.description: Not Judged is a real third answer, not a polite failure: the measure had no threshold, no usable value, or came from an instrument nobody uses.

fields.label: Sample
fields.description: How many documents this was computed from. A sample of zero is why a value can be blank rather than zero.

fields.label: Value (raw)
fields.description: Exactly what the threshold is judged against: a bare number, or a state word such as ok / expired / unknown, or blank when the measure had no sample. Written together with Value by one builder, so the pair cannot drift -- the display string carries units and is for reading, this one is for comparing.

fields.label: Key
fields.description: Stable identity. Evidence rows carry the same key, which is how a child table stands in for the grandchild table Frappe does not have.
